criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The purpose, Australian relevance, and broad user group are clear and supported by sources. However, objectives and requirements are not sufficiently specific: no target coverage, revisit, resolution, accuracy, or defined sensor and operational concept is given.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
Reef-monitoring satellites could also be used to report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: The Gantt chart and task descriptions give a feasible sequence, with relevant launch, orbit, ground, communications, and STK work. Information sources are listed. The plan does not explain contingencies or how schedule changes would be handled, and the schedule-to-mission rationale is only partly developed.

evidence.quote: I will need to choose an optimal orbit path and altitude, and also calculate COEs & AOEs.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Some useful background research and software familiarisation have been completed. However, no preliminary orbit, payload, link, or other technical design result is presented, and there is little interpretation of the work completed.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, in my progress, I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report has clear headings, readable prose, and a legible, labelled Gantt chart. The presentation is generally coherent, but some plan descriptions are informal or fragmentary and the references are presented mainly as bare URLs rather than a consistently formatted reference list.

evidence.quote: Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue. Deadlines are indicated by red lines.

technical_issues.issue: The report links ocean acidification directly to coral bleaching. Ocean acidification can stress reefs, but mass bleaching is primarily associated with elevated sea temperatures and heat stress; the causal explanation should distinguish these effects.

The proposed use of seafloor colour to detect bleaching is not technically established for a satellite mission. The cited Asner approach is not shown to transfer directly to satellite sensing; water depth, turbidity, atmospheric effects, and required spectral and spatial resolution would constrain detection.
No preliminary payload, orbit, coverage, revisit, or communications analysis is provided, so the near-real-time monitoring capability is not yet demonstrated.

overall: A clear and relevant Australian mission concept is supported by a workable schedule, listed sources, and selection of STK. The report needs more specific mission requirements and preliminary technical design evidence. Address the bleaching-causation claim and establish whether satellite sensing can reliably detect reef colour changes.

feedback.summary: You present a relevant Australian reef-monitoring concept, a feasible task sequence in Image 1, useful sources, and evidence of STK familiarisation. To reach the next rubric level, turn the broad concept into measurable mission requirements, add preliminary technical results that test whether the proposed monitoring is feasible, and strengthen contingencies and report referencing.
next_steps: In Mission Concept & Rationale, define measurable coverage, revisit, resolution, accuracy, sensor, and operational requirements. Distinguish ocean acidification from the heat stress that primarily drives mass bleaching, and assess whether satellite sensing can detect reef colour changes despite depth, turbidity, and atmospheric effects.
Build on Image 1 with contingency time or alternate actions for delays, and explain how each planned task and information source supports this mission. Show how schedule changes would be managed.

Use your STK tutorials and background research to produce and interpret preliminary payload, orbit, coverage, revisit, or communications results. Then edit for a consistently professional style and provide a properly formatted reference list that matches your in-text citations.

criteria.C1: Your Mission Concept & Rationale establishes Australian relevance, a broad user group, and the aim of near-real-time monitoring. For the next level, specify measurable objectives and requirements, and explain how users would use the data. Distinguish acidification from heat-driven bleaching and demonstrate that satellite sensing can detect reef colour changes under relevant conditions.
criteria.C2: Image 1 and your task descriptions provide a feasible sequence, and Useful Links identifies relevant sources. To reach the next level, explain why the sequence fits the mission and add contingencies for delays or changes, including how you would adjust the plan while completing the required design work.
criteria.C3: You have read about Asner’s monitoring system and completed STK tutorials 1–4, showing useful preparation. For the next level, present preliminary technical results—such as payload, orbit, coverage, revisit, or communications analysis—and briefly interpret what they show about the proposed near-real-time capability.
criteria.C4: Your report uses clear headings, readable prose, and a labelled, legible Gantt chart in Image 1. To reach the next level, make plan descriptions consistently polished, format references consistently rather than relying mainly on bare URLs, and ensure in-text citations and the reference list match.
